version.changelog: AI-powered video editing — turn raw footage into polished vlogs, highlight reels, TikTok/Shorts/Reels, montages, and more. Control the editing flow through Telegram chat, or let your ClawBot handle it automatically. Pick a style and let Sparki handle the rest, or describe what you want in your own words.

llm.summary: The skill's code and instructions mostly match a video-editing CLI that needs a Sparki API key, but there are inconsistencies (a dev API hostname, mixed install metadata, and an external installer suggestion) that warrant caution before installing.

dimensions.detail: Name/description (AI video editing) aligns with the included CLI code, commands (upload, edit, download), and the single primary credential (SPARKI_API_KEY). However the default API host in the code is agent-api-dev.aicoding.live (a dev/staging-sounding host) while the homepage metadata points to sparki.io — this mismatch is unexpected and should be verified with the publisher.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructions restrict operations to uploading/editing/downloading videos and explicitly instruct not to accept video files directly via chat. The instructions reference only declared config paths (~/.openclaw) and the Sparki CLI commands in the bundle; they do not ask for unrelated local data or unrelated credentials.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Registry said 'no install spec' but SKILL.md and scripts include an install step that requires the 'uv' binary and a scripts/setup.sh that runs 'uv sync'. The setup error message suggests installing 'uv' via a remote curl|sh (https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh). Requiring a third-party installer script (even only as user guidance) is higher-risk and the manifest/registry inconsistency is an engineering red flag.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Only SPARKI_API_KEY (primary) is required and the code respects a local config file (~/.openclaw/config/sparki.json). The code optionally reads SPARKI_UPLOAD_TG_LINK. No unrelated credentials (AWS, Google, etc.) are requested. The one concern is the default backend URL (agent-api-dev.aicoding.live) — an API key intended for sparki.io might expose data to a different host if left at defaults.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Skill does not set always:true, and only writes to its own config/history under ~/.openclaw (declared in metadata). It doesn't alter other skills or request elevated system-wide privileges.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This package mostly behaves like a normal Sparki CLI for video editing, but check a few things before installing: 1) Verify the API host — the code defaults to agent-api-dev.aicoding.live (looks like a dev/staging endpoint) while the homepage is sparki.io; confirm which backend your API key will talk to. 2) The bundle expects the 'uv' tool; the included setup script will call 'uv sync' and the error message suggests installing uv with a remote curl|sh — avoid running unfamiliar installers without review. 3) The CLI stores your SPARKI_API_KEY in ~/.openclaw/config/sparki.json if you run setup; treat that key like any secret and only use a key you trust for this host. 4) The registry metadata claimed 'no install spec' but code and scripts are present — that inconsistency suggests the package metadata may be stale or mis-published. If you want to proceed: test in an isolated environment, confirm the API base_url with the publisher, and avoid running remote install curl|sh commands unless you trust the source.
